newsitem.title: USA: Fed says tally of LA vault shows records accurate.
newsitem.headline: Fed says tally of LA vault shows records accurate.

text.p: The Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco on Monday said an audit of the vault at the bank's Los Angeles branch showed that its accounting of the cash held there was accurate.

"Over the past weekend, examiners for the Federal Reserve Board counted the coins and bills in the vault and their findings indicated that the physical inventory balances were consistent with the stated financial information," said Sandra Conlan, spokeswoman for the San Francisco Fed.
The unannounced visit by Fed board examiners was in addition to a separate review of the Los Angeles branch conducted by board examiners earlier this summer, Conlan said.

The Fed said the previous review showed sound accounting practices at the branch were sound despite some mistakes that the San Francisco Fed acknowledged in some of its statistical reports earlier this year.
The Fed said it has corrected those mistakes and that they have no bearing on the bank's financial position.
However, a draft report from the General Accounting Office, a congressional watchdog agency, was critical of the methods for counting cash at the Los Angeles branch.
